subject: SLA Exception Request: Approve 'Hold Rollforward' for model v21.2 (p95 drift)
messages:
From: Jane Holt <jane.holt@finlytics.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:17:00 -0000
Subject: Increase in p95 latency after v21.2 rollforward

Hi Rishi —

We pushed v21.2 to 3 of our production regions late Wednesday and are seeing a sustained p95 increase on text-generation routes (approx +320ms) starting 2026-09-10 02:40 UTC. User impact is only the SSO-backed endpoints for two high-volume customers but it's consistent across variants. Attached is the initial p95 report and a small KV-cache trace we pulled while reproducing.

Can you advise whether this is likely a model-level regression (changes in attention kernels / quant path) or a serving config difference? Our SRE team flagged that the increase correlates with sequences >512 tokens.

We need a short response with next steps in the hour if you can — our ERG wants to know whether to pin traffic back to v21.1 or to enable a temporary traffic cap.

Thanks,
Jane Holt
SRE Lead — FinLytics

Attachments: p95_report_v21.2.csv (csv), kv-cache-trace-20260912.txt (txt)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Holt <jane.holt@finlytics.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 15:32:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Increase in p95 latency after v21.2 rollforward — request: Hold rollforward

Team —

FinLytics reported a clear p95 regression after v21.2. Initial triage from our runtime team suggests the delta is in attention-kernel dispatch for long sequences and an interaction with the new KV prefetch path we shipped in v21.2. Monica and I ran a small repro in our canary and saw similar +280–350ms p95 increases for requests >512 tokens.

Ask: I need authorization to "Hold Rollforward" (i.e., prevent rollforward to additional regions and open a provisional SLA carveout for FinLytics) while we:
- Revert KV prefetch to prior behavior on the canary and measure p95 (expected 80–120ms drop)
- Produce an evidence pack (p95 bucketed by length + kernel traces) for FinLytics and Product
- Prepare a targeted variant (v21.2-kq) with the old prefetch and quant kernel fallback for long sequences as a fast fallback

Impact: Holding rollforward will keep current traffic distribution pinned to v21.1 in not-yet-rolled regions. We should be explicit with FinLytics that this is temporary and that we will be operating with a provisional SLA tolerance while we validate.

I request signoff from leadership on the carveout and authorization to send FinLytics an official mitigation plan.

--
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0132

Attachments referenced: grafana-snapshot-20260912.png
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 11:43:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Hold rollforward — operational suggestion

Rishi —

Agree with a hold, but prefer a scoped mitigation instead of a full pin for other customers. Proposal:

1) Immediate: Push a traffic cap (20% max burst) for v21.2 in at-risk regions and add a route-level prefix KV bypass for requests >512 tokens (config flag only) — this can be toggled without model redeploy.
2) Short-term (48 hrs): Revert the KV prefetch behavior in canary, validate p95 reduction, and run a traffic-split test (10% v21.2 vs 90% v21.1).
3) If canary shows >200ms reduction, approve a controlled rollforward with variant fallback; if not, rollback v21.2 entirely.

Also recommend we pre-approve a provisional SLA variance message and a 72-hour window to produce evidentiary logs for FinLytics. If leadership signs off I can coordinate the cap and the config toggle with infra.

Ben
Sr. Product Ops — Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Holt <jane.holt@finlytics.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -0000
Subject: Re: SLA Exception Request: Approve 'Hold Rollforward' for model v21.2 (p95 drift)

Thanks for the triage and clear plan. I approve the following, effective immediately:

- Authorize "Hold Rollforward" for v21.2 to prevent further region rollouts.
- Approve a provisional SLA variance for FinLytics for up to 72 hours while the infra/runtime team validates the KV prefetch revert in canary. Legal/CS should be looped with the template I cc'd below.
- Authorize Ben to apply the traffic cap and the route-level prefix KV bypass toggle as a lower-impact mitigation — do that first while the revert runs.

Please notify FinLytics that we are taking these steps and provide an ETA for the 48-hour validation. Important: capture the evidence pack (p95 by token-length, kernel dispatch logs, KV traces) and attach to the FinLytics ticket and the DL-98123 deal in the partner tracker.

Kimberly Park
VP, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
